newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish bank upgrades Telepizza to buy.
newsitem.headline: Spanish bank upgrades Telepizza to buy.

text.p: Spanish bank BBV said on Thursday it had upgraded its recommendation on Telepizza to "buy" from "neutral" on the back of the share price and profit forecasts for the pizza delivery chain.
In a research report, the bank said it had also upwardly revised its 1997 results forecasts for Telepizza after a dazzling performance so far this year.
BBV said it had raised forecasts for net profit to 2.51 billion pesetas from 2.42 billion for the year, while it expected an ordinary profit of 3.98 billion pesetas.
"We are revising upward our forecasts for 1997 results, as a result of the growth in sales and a better than expected trend in the sales margin," BBV said in its research report.

BBV said it had raised its average sales forecasts per shop to a fall of 0.6 percent from a fall of 1.4 percent to give a group sales figures of 39 billion pesetas. The fall per shop is due to Telepizza's recent purchase of rival chain PizzaWorld which added another 109 shops to its network.

BBV said it had also increased its target price for the stock at the end of the year to 10,000 pesetas from 9,500 pesetas, giving a price to earnings ratio objective of 42.7 times forecast results for 1997.
On Thursday, Telepizza shares were trading 50 pesetas up at 8,900.
In the first half, Telepizza announced its net profit had risen to 1.03 billion pesetas from 0.71 billion a year earlier. Sales rose 37.6 percent to 17.50 billion pesetas.
BBV and Transeuropean Research Traders, which is controlled by Telepizza chairman Leopoldo Fernandez Pujals, hold 44 percent of Telepizza.
